overclaims: That supports the claim that the investor-reported margin fell short of expectations.
checks.note: The excerpt, proposition, outcome and citation match the case. The problem is the rationale's 'investor-reported margin'. The Decoder excerpt and its surrounding text say only that the 2025 adjusted gross margin was 33% against a 46% target. Nothing in e1 says the figure came from an investor presentation or was reported to investors. That link comes from Zitron's quotation of The Information, not from the evidence. The rationale should describe the margin as The Decoder's reported adjusted gross margin, without the investor attribution.

The public excerpt for e1 cuts the frozen exact words down to 'She has been reporting to Simo, not him, since August 2025.' That drops 'The Information reports that Altman has excluded Friar from key financial meetings.' Two problems follow. The exclusion, which the rationale and e1's explanation depend on, is no longer in the published excerpt. And without the attribution to The Information, the reporting-line claim reads as Om Malik's own. The fix is to publish both sentences in full. The rest of the payload is faithful.
